correctness.rationale: For interior x the deterministic zero equation is C=A/x+B/(1−x), whose minimum is the stated fold; the quadratic sign gives stability of r+. Integrating the factored quadratic to r+ gives Ψ(r+)/w=C r+²(r+−3r−)/6. The height is negative at the fold, rises strictly because ∂C D=x(1−x), and becomes positive as r+ tends to 1 and the C term dominates the integral. The root-ratio condition and Vieta give the larger stated solution for √C. At stationarity, q+(0)=μ and q−(N)=μ. In the interior write q+=x(1−x)σ(wD)[1+μ/(x σ(wD))] and similarly q− with 1−x and σ(−wD); summing the logarithmic corrections gives O(μ N log N). Telescoping the x(1−x) factors and the one-step logistic arguments gives π(k)/π(0) comparable uniformly to μ exp(N Ψ(k/N))/[x(1−x)], including the O(1) Riemann error for fixed parameters. The far endpoint has at most an extra O(N) relative to its nearest interior state and a strict exponential deficit against the maximum. At equal height a boundary layer next to zero contributes O(μ N), and the interior quadratic maximum contributes O(μ √N), both relative to π(0), with exponentially small remainder. These vanish for μ=N⁻² and prove boundary selection, not just the large-deviation tie. Away from the tie the unique potential maximum wins exponentially. The symmetric example follows by substitution. The limitations' wording about needing exactly N⁻² should be read as identifying the scale of the theorem, not as a necessity result: for example the same comparison at N⁻³ also selects zero. The frozen finite diagnostics were inspected, not run or treated as proof.

value.rationale: The two thresholds answer different natural questions in a payoff family already used to model explosive cooperation. Their exact separation gives a nonempty interval, when accessible, in which deterministic cooperative attraction fails to predict the large-population stationary outcome. Resolving equal heights by finite-weight asymptotics distinguishes this from a routine computation of the deterministic roots or a bare large-deviation maximizer. The conclusion is for the specified closure, not evidence for a hypergraph process it does not model.
